```ein
;;; Ein — the Zebra puzzle in the text's own words: one relation a verb.
;;;
;;; The statements are the sentences of the puzzle, each one fact whose
;;; relation is the sentence's verb and whose arguments are the words it
;;; names: *The Ukrainian drinks tea* is `(drinks Ukrainian Tea)`, *Coffee is
;;; drunk in the green house* is `(is-drunk-in Coffee Green)`. The two
;;; questions are one query in the statements' own relations, `(drinks ?who
;;; Water)` and `(owns ?who Zebra)`.
;;;
;;; What a sentence describes rather than names is written as the word the
;;; description is built on:
;;;
;;;   the red house                         Red, the house of the colour
;;;   the first house, the middle house     First, Middle: the houses are
;;;                                         named by their places in the row
;;;   the Old Gold smoker                   Old_Gold, the man of the brand
;;;   the man who smokes Chesterfields      Chesterfields
;;;   the man with the fox                  Fox
;;;   the house where the horse is kept     Horse
;;;
;;; so `(owns Old_Gold Snail)` reads *the Old Gold smoker owns snails* only to
;;; a reader who knows that a man and the brand he smokes share a house. A
;;; noun is written once for all its forms: *snails* is `Snail`, *Parliaments*
;;; `Parliament`, *orange juice* `Juice`.
;;;
;;; The file is written in the order a formalization makes it: the
;;; statements in the text's order, each with its sentence as `:source`, and
;;; the questions; then the ontology, the relations and what kind of thing
;;; each name is; then the theory, what the library brings and the facts that
;;; select it. A fact may come before its relation's declaration and a
;;; selecting fact before the import that brings its rule.
;;;
;;; A sentence keeps its voice: *Coffee is drunk in the green house* is a
;;; passive of place, `is-drunk-in`, and *The Ukrainian drinks tea* an active,
;;; `drinks`.
;;;
;;; The theory is the library's, and the file writes no rule. Every verb of a
;;; shared house is a part of one relation, `same-house`, which std.slots
;;; makes an equivalence whose classes are the houses; every verb of a neighbour
;;; is a part of `next-to`. The hypotheses are std.slots' obligations: each
;;; value owes a house, each house a value of each kind.
;;; The verbs are related as the language relates them: an active and its
;;; passive are converses, `(drinks ?man ?drink)` and `(is-drunk-by ?drink
;;; ?man)`, each read from the other; a passive of place goes through the man
;;; who lives in the house, a drink being drunk in the house of the man it is
;;; drunk by; and a value placed in a house is in it by the verb of its kind.
;;; That is how the questions, asked in `drinks` and `owns`, are answered.
;;;
;;; Answer: the Norwegian drinks water; the Japanese owns the zebra.
;;; examples/README.md § Zebra puzzle compares it with the other encodings.


;; ──── The statements ───────────────────────────────────────────

;; *There are five houses* names five things of one kind, and no more.
(instance First  House :source "There are five houses.")
(instance Second House :source "There are five houses.")
(instance Middle House :source "There are five houses.")
(instance Fourth House :source "There are five houses.")
(instance Fifth  House :source "There are five houses.")

(lives-in    Englishman Red         :source "The Englishman lives in the red house.")
(owns        Spaniard   Dog         :source "The Spaniard owns the dog.")
(is-drunk-in Coffee     Green       :source "Coffee is drunk in the green house.")
(drinks      Ukrainian  Tea         :source "The Ukrainian drinks tea.")
(is-immediately-to-the-right-of Green Ivory
  :source "The green house is immediately to the right of the ivory house.")
(owns        Old_Gold   Snail       :source "The Old Gold smoker owns snails.")
(are-smoked-in Kools    Yellow      :source "Kools are smoked in the yellow house.")
(is-drunk-in Milk       Middle      :source "Milk is drunk in the middle house.")
(lives-in    Norwegian  First       :source "The Norwegian lives in the first house.")
(lives-next-to Chesterfields Fox
  :source "The man who smokes Chesterfields lives in the house next to the man with the fox.")
(are-smoked-next-to Kools Horse
  :source "Kools are smoked in the house next to the house where the horse is kept.")
(drinks      Lucky_Strike Juice     :source "The Lucky Strike smoker drinks orange juice.")
(smokes      Japanese   Parliament  :source "The Japanese smokes Parliaments.")
(lives-next-to Norwegian Blue       :source "The Norwegian lives next to the blue house.")

;; *Who drinks water? Who owns the zebra?*
(query
  :goal (and (drinks ?who_water Water) (owns ?who_zebra Zebra))
  :goal-text "The {?who_water} drinks water. The {?who_zebra} owns the zebra.")


;; ──── The ontology ─────────────────────────────────────────────

;; The verbs, each with the words its sentences put in its places.
(relation lives-in       Man House       :why "a {?3} lives in a {?4}")
(relation owns           Man Pet         :why "a {?3} owns a {?4}")
(relation is-drunk-in    Drink House     :why "a {?3} is drunk in a {?4}")
(relation drinks         Man Drink       :why "a {?3} drinks a {?4}")
(relation are-smoked-in  Cigarette House :why "{?3}s are smoked in a {?4}")
(relation smokes         Man Cigarette   :why "a {?3} smokes {?4}s")
(relation is-immediately-to-the-right-of House House
  :why "a {?3} is immediately to the right of a {?4}")
(relation lives-next-to  Man Man         :why "a {?3} lives in the house next to a {?4}")
(relation are-smoked-next-to Cigarette House
  :why "{?3}s are smoked in the house next to a {?4}")

;; Their passives, and the verb a pet's place is said in, which the text uses
;; only inside a description (*the house where the horse is kept*).
(relation is-drunk-by    Drink Man       :why "a {?3} is drunk by a {?4}")
(relation are-smoked-by  Cigarette Man   :why "{?3}s are smoked by a {?4}")
(relation is-owned-by    Pet Man         :why "a {?3} is owned by a {?4}")
(relation is-lived-in-by House Man       :why "a {?3} is lived in by a {?4}")
(relation is-kept-in     Pet House       :why "a {?3} is kept in a {?4}")

;; What the theory reads the verbs into, and the kinds.
(relation same-house     Attribute Attribute :why "a {?3} and a {?4} are in the same house")
(relation next-to        Attribute Attribute :why "a {?3}'s house is next to a {?4}'s")
(relation man-and-house       Nationality House :why "a {?3} and a {?4}")
(relation drink-and-house     Drink House       :why "a {?3} and a {?4}")
(relation cigarette-and-house Cigarette House   :why "a {?3} and a {?4}")
(relation pet-and-house       Pet House         :why "a {?3} and a {?4}")
(relation instance       T T                 :why "{?3} is a {?4}")
(relation type           T T                 :why "{?3} is a kind of {?4}")

(type Attribute   T)
(type House       Attribute)
(type Color       Attribute)
(type Nationality Attribute)
(type Drink       Attribute)
(type Cigarette   Attribute)
(type Pet         Attribute)
(instance Red    Color) (instance Green Color) (instance Ivory Color)
(instance Yellow Color) (instance Blue  Color)
(instance Englishman Nationality) (instance Spaniard  Nationality)
(instance Ukrainian  Nationality) (instance Norwegian Nationality)
(instance Japanese   Nationality)
(instance Coffee Drink) (instance Tea   Drink) (instance Milk Drink)
(instance Juice  Drink) (instance Water Drink)
(instance Old_Gold      Cigarette) (instance Kools        Cigarette)
(instance Chesterfields Cigarette) (instance Lucky_Strike Cigarette)
(instance Parliament    Cigarette)
(instance Dog   Pet) (instance Snail Pet) (instance Fox Pet)
(instance Horse Pet) (instance Zebra Pet)

;; The row the text speaks of, *the first*, *the middle*, *to the right of*,
;; *next to*, and never states.
(is-immediately-to-the-right-of Second First)
(is-immediately-to-the-right-of Middle Second)
(is-immediately-to-the-right-of Fourth Middle)
(is-immediately-to-the-right-of Fifth  Fourth)


;; ──── The theory ───────────────────────────────────────────────

(import std.algebra :symbols (symmetric includes converse compose top meet))
(import std.slots)

;; Whether an explanation searches every derivation of a fact for the smallest
;; core. One link re-derived many ways (each verb, the symmetry, std.slots'
;; placements all reach one pair) makes that search cost minutes for a state
;; the run decides in milliseconds, wherever a dead state's core is printed
;; (`--events`, `--dump-lattice`); off, a core is taken from the derivation
;; recorded first. It changes which core is named, and no state.
(config :record-alternative-justifications false)

;; A verb of a shared house is a part of `same-house`, a verb of a neighbour
;; a part of `next-to`: `(includes drinks same-house)` copies every `drinks`
;; fact into `same-house`.
(includes lives-in      same-house)
(includes owns          same-house)
(includes is-drunk-in   same-house)
(includes drinks        same-house)
(includes are-smoked-in same-house)
(includes smokes        same-house)
(includes is-immediately-to-the-right-of next-to)
(includes lives-next-to      next-to)
(includes are-smoked-next-to next-to)
(symmetric same-house)
(symmetric next-to)

;; `same-house`'s classes are the houses, each holding one value of every
;; kind, and a house names its class; the two relations of a row hold
;; between values exactly where they hold between their houses.
(slot-partition same-house instance type Attribute House)
(slot-spatial   same-house is-immediately-to-the-right-of instance House)
(slot-spatial   same-house next-to instance House)

;; A verb's active and passive are converses: what a man drinks is drunk by
;; him. One fact a pair, which the library reads both ways
;; (`converse-pair-symmetric`).
(converse drinks   is-drunk-by)
(converse smokes   are-smoked-by)
(converse owns     is-owned-by)
(converse lives-in is-lived-in-by)

;; A passive of place goes through the man who lives there: a drink is drunk
;; in the house of the man it is drunk by, and by the man who lives in the
;; house it is drunk in; the same for cigarettes, and for a pet, kept where
;; its owner lives.
(compose is-drunk-by   lives-in       is-drunk-in)
(compose is-drunk-in   is-lived-in-by is-drunk-by)
(compose are-smoked-by lives-in       are-smoked-in)
(compose are-smoked-in is-lived-in-by are-smoked-by)
(compose is-owned-by   lives-in       is-kept-in)
(compose is-kept-in    is-lived-in-by is-owned-by)

;; Where a value is, in the verb of its kind: a man lives in the house he
;; shares, a drink is drunk in it, cigarettes are smoked in it, a pet is kept
;; in it.
(top  man-and-house       instance Nationality House)
(meet same-house man-and-house       lives-in)
(top  drink-and-house     instance Drink House)
(meet same-house drink-and-house     is-drunk-in)
(top  cigarette-and-house instance Cigarette House)
(meet same-house cigarette-and-house are-smoked-in)
(top  pet-and-house       instance Pet House)
(meet same-house pet-and-house       is-kept-in)
```

```ein
;;; Ann is older than Bob. Bob is older than Cy. Who is the youngest?
;;;
;;; Step 3, the complete program: step 2's program, the rules the library
;;; does not have, each saying what it asks the calculator and what it reads
;;; back, and the hypothesis mechanism.


;; ──── The statements ───────────────────────────────────────────

;; Ann is older than Bob.
(older Ann Bob :source "Ann is older than Bob.")

;; Bob is older than Cy.
(older Bob Cy :source "Bob is older than Cy.")

;; *Who is the youngest?*
(query :goal (youngest ?who) :goal-text "{?who} is the youngest")


;; ──── The ontology ─────────────────────────────────────────────

(relation older Person Person :why "a {?3} is older than a {?4}")
(relation person Person :why "{?3} is a person")
(relation youngest Person :why "a {?3} is the youngest")


;; ──── The theory ───────────────────────────────────────────────

;; Synthesised: of two who are persons, the one who is older than the other
;; is the youngest if the other is older than nobody.
(rule youngest-is-older-than-nobody ()
  :match  (and (person ?p) (absent (older ?p ?q)))
  :assert (youngest ?p)
  :why    "{?p} is older than nobody, so {?p} is the youngest")

;; The hypothesis mechanism: none; the text states every fact there is.
(solve :no-search)
```
